# Open Civic Web

> Free, nonpartisan, plain-language public records of local government across Florida: city and county
> governing boards statewide (see "What we cover in Florida"), including the Temple Terrace City Council, the
> Hillsborough, Pasco and Hernando county commissions (which govern Brandon, Lutz, Wesley Chapel and Spring Hill)
> and, in southeast Volusia County, the Edgewater City Council and the Oak Hill City Commission, where the project
> began. Collected nightly from official sources; every record links to its source.
> Headlines are produced by fixed rules, not AI, and the official wording is always shown.

Pages count recorded votes; they never say why anyone voted or whether a decision was good. Hillsborough votes
come from the Clerk's Master Voting Record (2014 on); Pasco and Temple Terrace votes are read from the Clerk's minutes;
Hernando and Edgewater votes come from their Legistar records. New Smyrna Beach isn't collected: its records site asks
automated tools not to. Other Florida governments (see "What we cover in Florida") come from their Legistar records
(meetings, agenda items and each member's vote) or their CivicClerk portals (meetings and agenda items only).

- [Public money to companies](https://bgraham1214.github.io/open-civic/companies.html): companies and organizations the governments agreed to pay (contracts, purchases, change orders, grants), decision by decision, with approved amounts (not payments) and factual flags (no competitive bidding, money added to a contract, approved over a no vote, $1 million or more on consent, conflict-of-interest abstentions)
- [Top companies](https://bgraham1214.github.io/open-civic/top-companies.html): the ten companies with the most money approved and the ten with the most contracts since January 2025, for every government we follow with votes, each county, and each government
- [Florida at a glance](https://bgraham1214.github.io/open-civic/at-a-glance.html): subjects coming up in many governments at once in the last 90 days (data centers, license-plate cameras, property tax rates and more), each with every government that took it up; one page per subject under issues/
- [Spotlight](https://bgraham1214.github.io/open-civic/spotlight.html): decisions tagged by fixed rules as new restrictions (bans, moratoriums, fines) or as money, land or breaks for companies (tax breaks, incentives, land sales and leases, no-bid purchases of $100,000 or more)
